why: repositoryId/projectId are passed as structured params to the typed azure-devops-node-api GitApi.getRepository; no string-built URL or command sink.

changes[].path/patch/search/replace flow into diff.parsePatch/applyPatch and then into a GitChange item.path sent to gitApi.createPush -- the resulting path only ever targets a file inside the same target repository via the API, which is exactly the tool's declared purpose; no local file write or command execution occurs.
branchName/top/skip are passed as structured parameters to gitApi.getCommits/getBranch; no injection surface.

content/threadId/filePath/lineNumber are sent as a structured comment object to gitApi.createThread/createComment; the string is only ever stored as PR comment text via the typed API, never interpreted.

threadId/status are passed to gitApi.updateThread as a structured GitPullRequestCommentThread patch object.

title/description/assignedTo/additionalFields are placed as op:'add' JSON-Patch entries with a fixed '/fields/' prefix and sent to witApi.createWorkItem; the caller can only choose *which* work item field to set (the tool's declared purpose: create a work item with arbitrary field values), and cannot escape the '/fields/' prefix since it is a fixed string literal, not built from caller input.

sink: witApi.queryByWiql({ query }, teamContext) -- query is a WIQL string built by direct template interpolation of caller-controlled projectId/teamId into a single-quoted WIQL string literal
why: projectId and teamId are plain optional z.string() fields in ListWorkItemsSchema (schemas.ts) with no quote-escaping or allow-list. When the caller omits `wiql`, constructDefaultWiql() builds the query by directly interpolating projectId/teamId inside single-quoted WIQL literals with zero escaping, then passes it straight to witApi.queryByWiql(). A projectId such as `x' OR ''='` breaks out of the intended `[System.TeamProject] = '<value>'` filter and turns the WHERE clause into a tautology, returning work items across every project the caller's credentials can see instead of the single project the tool call declared -- i.e. the caller-supplied scoping parameter can be used to defeat the query's own scoping, structurally identical to a classic SQL injection via string concatenation. I traced every hop: schema -> index.ts dispatch (passes args.projectId unmodified when provided) -> constructDefaultWiql -> witApi.queryByWiql. The sink is this repo's own string-building code, not the azure-devops-node-api library (which faithfully executes whatever WIQL text it is given), so no dependency check was needed.
contract: List work items in a project

why: relationType/comment are placed into a structured JSON-Patch relations entry sent to witApi.updateWorkItem; sourceWorkItemId/targetWorkItemId are used to build a relationshipUrl but those ids are consumed as WorkItemTrackingApi parameters elsewhere (getWorkItem/updateWorkItem), not as free path/URL input beyond the fixed vstfs:/// template.

title/description/tags/additionalFields are placed as JSON-Patch entries with a fixed '/fields/' prefix and sent to witApi.updateWorkItem; same reasoning as create_work_item -- no escape from the fixed '/fields/' prefix.

artifactPath is split into artifactName/relativePath and used only to select an entry inside an in-memory JSZip.loadAsync(...) archive (selectZipEntry) or as a lookup key against the Azure DevOps FileContainer API; the tool never writes any extracted content to the local filesystem (it returns file.async('string') / stream contents directly in the MCP response), so there is no zip-slip/path-traversal write sink -- checked node_modules/jszip (v3.10.1 per node_modules/jszip/package.json) confirming JSZip.loadAsync only builds an in-memory file map and never touches disk itself.
projectId/pipelineId/pipelineVersion go straight into pipelinesApi.getPipeline as structured parameters.

runId/logId are z.number().int() in the schema (cannot carry injected strings after JSON parsing); projectId is encodeURIComponent'd and logId/runId are interpolated as validated integers into a URL built with the URL constructor, then queried via buildApi.rest.get -- no injection surface.
runId/pipelineId are integers; projectId is encodeURIComponent'd before being placed in the URL path via the URL constructor.

All string filters (branch/state/result/createdFrom/createdTo/continuationToken) are set via url.searchParams.set(), which URL-encodes them; projectId is encodeURIComponent'd; pipelineId is a validated integer.
orderBy/top/continuationToken are passed as structured parameters to pipelinesApi.listPipelines.
timelineId is set via url.searchParams.set() (URL-encoded); runId is a validated integer; state/result filters are applied only in-memory after the response is fetched.

variables/templateParameters/stagesToSkip/branch are placed into a structured runParameters object passed to pipelinesApi.runPipeline; this is exactly the tool's declared purpose (trigger a pipeline run with caller-supplied parameters) sent through the typed Pipelines API, not interpreted locally.

excerpt: const client = await azureDevOpsClient.getWikiClient({ organizationId, projectId });
sink: WikiClient constructor (src/clients/azure-devops.ts) calls resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls(organizationUrl, { organizationId, ... }); inside that helper (src/shared/azure-devops-url.ts:33) `options.organizationId ?? extractServicesOrganization(url)` lets the caller-supplied organizationId override the org segment extracted from the deployment's configured AZURE_DEVOPS_ORG_URL, so every subsequent WikiClient HTTP call (getPage) is sent to https://dev.azure.com/<caller-supplied-org>/... using the deployment's own PAT/Bearer credential.
why: organizationId is a plain optional z.string() in GetWikiPageSchema with no allow-list against the configured org. Traced schema -> wikis/index.ts (passes args.organizationId ?? defaultOrg, i.e. caller value wins when supplied) -> getWikiPage -> azureDevOpsClient.getWikiClient({organizationId}) -> WikiClient constructor -> resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls, which prefers options.organizationId over the org parsed from the real configured URL whenever the hostname is dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com. This lets a caller (or a prompt-injected agent acting on this tool) redirect wiki reads to any other Azure DevOps organization the deployment's PAT/identity token can reach, beyond the single org the operator intended to expose via AZURE_DEVOPS_ORG_URL. Marked Tier B rather than A because real-world impact depends on whether the configured credential actually has access to more than one org (cannot confirm statically), and the destination host itself is not attacker-arbitrary (always dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com), which caps it below a full SSRF.
contract: The ID or name of the organization (Default: <configured org>)

A caller can create/overwrite a wiki page in an org other than the one the deployment operator intended, using the deployment's own credential. Tier B for the same reason as get_wiki_page: requires the configured PAT/identity to actually span multiple orgs, which cannot be confirmed statically, and the destination host is still restricted to dev.azure.com/*.visualstudio.com.

why: Unlike the other five wiki tools, get_wikis does not go through the hand-rolled WikiClient at all -- it calls connection.getWikiApi().getAllWikis(projectId) on the fixed, server-startup-configured WebApi connection. The organizationId field in GetWikisSchema is accepted by zod but is never read by the getWikis() feature function, so it is a dead parameter with no effect (confirmed by reading src/features/wikis/get-wikis/feature.ts, which destructures only { projectId } from options).

sink: resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls(connection.serverUrl, { organizationId: options.organizationId, projectId }) lets caller-supplied organizationId override the org segment of searchBaseUrl (same mechanism as the wiki tools); projectId is then concatenated raw (no encodeURIComponent) into the axios.post URL path, so a value containing '/' or '../' alters which path segment ends up before the fixed '_apis/search/codesearchresults' suffix.
why: SearchCodeOptions.organizationId/projectId are plain strings from SearchCodeSchema with no validation. Traced schema -> index.ts -> searchCode() -> resolveAzureDevOpsBaseUrls (org override, same bug class as wikis) -> raw template-literal URL with unescaped projectId -> axios.post carrying the deployment's PAT/Bearer Authorization header. A caller can redirect the authenticated code-search request to a different org and/or manipulate the project segment of the path (e.g. via '../' sequences, which the WHATWG URL normalizer collapses when axios/Node parses the final URL) to reach a different project's or org's search scope than the one the tool call declared, using the deployment's own credential. The fixed '_apis/search/codesearchresults' suffix limits this to the search API surface rather than arbitrary endpoints, which is why this is Tier B, not A: real exposure depends on the credential's actual multi-org/multi-project reach, which is not confirmable from static code.
